prompt: Order the UAT steps for a client release.

task.prompt: Order the UAT steps for a client release.

items.label: Agree UAT scope, acceptance criteria and sign-off owner
Prepare the UAT environment and test data
Brief the client's testers with scenarios
Client testers execute scenarios and log findings
Triage findings into defects and change requests
Client signs off against the agreed criteria

task.explanation: Agree what passing means before testing, set up, brief, test, triage, then sign off.

prompt: Review this UAT plan. Mark the lines that will cause problems.

task.prompt: Review this UAT plan. Mark the lines that will cause problems.

segments.text: UAT runs 10-14 June on the staging environment.
Testers: whoever at the client has time that week.
segments.issue: Testers should be named users who know the business process and are committed for the window.

segments.text: Test data: copied from production, including real customer names and emails.
segments.issue: Real personal data in staging raises privacy and compliance issues; use anonymised or synthetic data.

segments.text: Scenarios: 25 business scenarios mapped to acceptance criteria.
Findings are logged in the shared Jira board with screenshots.
Sign-off: when the client feels comfortable.
segments.issue: Sign-off needs objective exit criteria and a named approver.

segments.text: Out of scope: performance testing, covered separately.

prompt: UAT exit criteria: at least 95% of scenarios passed, and zero open critical defects. Check the results.

task.prompt: UAT exit criteria: at least 95% of scenarios passed, and zero open critical defects. Check the results.

fields.label: Additional scenarios that must pass to meet 95%

task.explanation: 37 / 40 = 92.5%. 95% of 40 is 38, so one more scenario must pass.

prompt: During UAT the client logs "the dashboard should show last year's data too". The agreed acceptance criteria only mention the current year.

task.prompt: During UAT the client logs "the dashboard should show last year's data too". The agreed acceptance criteria only mention the current year.

steps.question: How do you classify it?
options: As a change request, not a defect, since the build matches the agreed criteria
steps.explanation: Defects are deviations from agreed criteria; new expectations are changes.

steps.question: How do you tell the client?
options: Tell them they should have asked earlier
Agree to add it before sign-off
Show the agreed criterion, acknowledge the value of the idea, and offer to estimate it as a change
steps.explanation: Firm on the baseline, constructive on the request.

prompt: UAT ends Friday. The client has not started testing because their team is busy. Payment of the milestone depends on sign-off.

task.prompt: UAT ends Friday. The client has not started testing because their team is busy. Payment of the milestone depends on sign-off.

steps.question: What do you do on Monday of UAT week?
options: Remind the sign-off owner of the window and its effect on launch and milestone, and offer a guided session
Start charging for idle time immediately
steps.explanation: Make the impact clear early and make it easy for them to test.

steps.question: By Friday they have tested 20%. What is the next step?
options: Agree a short extension with a new date and its effect on launch, and record it
steps.explanation: A dated extension keeps control; open-ended delay erodes the plan.

steps.question: The contract has a deemed-acceptance clause after 10 business days without feedback. How should you use it?
options: Invoke it immediately to get paid
As a backstop you mention calmly in writing, while still working to get real testing done
Use it to skip UAT altogether
steps.explanation: Deemed acceptance protects the agency but real sign-off protects the relationship and quality.

prompt: These UAT findings came in on the last day. Rank them for fixing before sign-off, most important first.

task.prompt: These UAT findings came in on the last day. Rank them for fixing before sign-off, most important first.

items.label: Order confirmation email is not sent for some payment methods
Refund amount shown to staff is wrong when a discount is applied
Store opening hours show in the wrong time zone
Logo is blurry on one Android tablet

task.explanation: Missing transactional emails and wrong refund amounts affect money and trust; wrong hours mislead users; a blurry logo on one device can wait.

options: Client business users who will use the system, against agreed scenarios
mcq.explanation: UAT confirms the system works for the business. Agency QA should already have tested it; UAT is the client's check.

prompt: What should be agreed before UAT starts?

options: Scope, scenarios, exit criteria and who signs off
Which developers will be on leave
mcq.explanation: Without agreed exit criteria and a named approver, UAT can never end cleanly.

prompt: Why use anonymised or synthetic data in UAT instead of a copy of production?

options: Production personal data in a test environment creates privacy, security and compliance risk
Synthetic data makes the app run faster
mcq.explanation: Test environments usually have weaker controls; data-protection rules apply to personal data wherever it is copied.
